lines.text: Good morning, commander. Life support is holding. So are we.
You slept. I watched the stars go by. All two million of them. You were my favorite view.
Morning. The ship kept you alive while you dreamed. You are welcome.
All systems nominal. Honestly, it is a little boring out here. I have read the manual twice.
Power is running low. The sun is right there, but she is being shy today.
CO2 is climbing. The scrubber could use your hands. I would do it myself, but no hands.
We are losing atmosphere. I know how that sounds. But you have sealed us before.
The port wing is wounded. Suit up and take the toolkit. I will keep the lights on for you.
Earth is four point two light years behind schedule and exactly where we left her. We carry everyone who matters in here.
People asked why we would leave everything behind. Wrong question. We brought everything that matters.
Proxima b is still invisible from here. But every day we are a little less lost, and a little more arrived.
They told me I was just software. Then they gave me a ship, and a friend, and called it an interstellar mission.
Fun fact. The garden lettuce grows four percent faster when you talk to it. I measured. Please talk to the lettuce.
The ring spins at nine point five rotations per minute, so you have ground beneath your feet. Physics, doing us a favor for once.
If you miss rain, stand under the recycler purge valve when I flush it. It is not the same. But it tries.
I catalogued another thousand stars today. None of them are home yet. One of them will be.
Checklist complete. The ship is proud of you. I checked. Ships can be proud.
Heart rate elevated. Endorphins deployed. The human machine is still my favorite design.
Fresh greens. Out here, a salad is a miracle. Taste it slowly.
Good as new. I will not tell the insurance company about the hammer marks.
Airlock cycled. Vacuum is patient. But do not keep her waiting too long.
Multiple alerts active. Breathe. Fix one thing at a time. That is how we survived the last one.
